problem_summary.summary: Evaluate a valid arithmetic expression written in postfix notation using integer arithmetic.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: tokens containing integer operands and +, -, *, or /. Return the integer expression value.
constraints: The expression is valid and has no division by zero
All intermediate values fit in signed 32-bit integers

brute_force.explanation: Use a dynamic list as a value stack. Push numeric tokens; when an operator arrives, remove the last two values in right-then-left order, evaluate, and push the result.
brute_force.correctness_idea: In postfix notation, an operator applies to the two most recent unevaluated expressions. The second popped value is its left operand and the first is its right operand, so reducing each token leaves the value of the processed prefix on the list.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) for n tokens; each token is processed once and list-end operations are amortized O(1).

optimized.explanation: Use a primitive int array as the operand stack to avoid boxing and dynamic-list overhead. Apply each operator to the top two values in operand order.
optimized.correctness_idea: The stack invariant is the same postfix reduction invariant: it stores completed operand subexpressions in order. Replacing the top two with their operation result preserves the value of the processed expression prefix.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) for n tokens, with one pass.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) for the primitive operand stack.

edge_cases.case: Subtraction and division are not commutative
edge_cases.handling: The first popped value is treated as right operand and the second as left operand.
Java integer division truncates toward zero, matching the requirement.
The sole stack value is returned directly.
